summary: Fundamental units of text processing in LLMs, with critical implications for cost, context limits, and performance

content.overview: Tokens are the fundamental units LLMs use to process text - not words or characters, but subword pieces. The tokenization process splits text into tokens using model-specific algorithms (BPE, WordPiece, etc.). Critical insight: Tokens directly determine (1) API costs (charged per token), (2) context window usage (counted in tokens), and (3) processing speed (more tokens = slower). Rough approximation: 1 token ≈ 0.75 words or 4 characters in English, but this varies by language and content type. CRITICAL: Always use the provider's official tokenizer for accurate counting - estimates can be off by 20-30%.
keyPoints: Tokens are MODEL-SPECIFIC - OpenAI, Anthropic, Google use different tokenizers; same text produces different token counts across providers
CRITICAL COST IMPLICATION: LLM API pricing is per-token - 10% increase in average tokens at 100M tokens/day = $1.5M/year additional cost
Common tokenization: 1 token ≈ 0.75 words (English), but varies significantly by language (Chinese/Japanese: ~1 char/token, code: highly variable)
Token count includes EVERYTHING: System prompt + user message + assistant response + tool definitions + tool results - all consume token budget
Use official tokenizers for accurate counting: tiktoken (OpenAI), Anthropic tokenizer (Claude), provider APIs - NOT character-based estimates
Cost optimization strategies: (1) Concise prompts (30-50% savings), (2) Caching repeated content (75-90% savings), (3) Template reuse, (4) Prune few-shot examples
Pre-flight token checks: Count tokens BEFORE API calls to prevent failures and control costs - fail fast when limits exceeded

examples.title: Cost Optimization via Concise Prompts
examples.explanation: Concise prompts cut token count 30-50% without sacrificing quality - massive cost savings at scale

warnings: NEVER use character-based token estimates for production - can be off by 20-30%, causing budget overruns or context failures
Tokenization is language-dependent - non-English text (especially logographic languages) uses significantly more tokens per word
Special characters and code are tokenized unpredictably - emojis, Unicode, formatted code can explode token counts
Changing tokenizer (e.g., model upgrade) changes token counts for same text - breaks budgets and context calculations
Hidden token costs: Tool definitions, system prompts, JSON schemas all consume tokens - not just user messages
Token limits are HARD boundaries - exceeding context window causes request failures, not graceful degradation
bestPractices: Implement pre-flight token counting in production - count tokens before API calls, reject requests exceeding budget
Use caching for repeated content (system prompts, tool definitions) - 75-90% cost reduction for cached tokens
Monitor token usage metrics: Average tokens/request, peak usage, cost per conversation - set alerts at thresholds
Template system prompts and reuse - avoids recounting and enables caching across requests
Prune few-shot examples and verbose instructions - typically saves 20-30% tokens without quality loss
Budget tokens across all inputs: System prompt + history + current query + tool results + reserve for output
Test token counts across different content types (code, prose, multilingual) - identify high-cost patterns
